title: PSWSMan Test Settings
description: WinRM servers the Pester connection tests can use. Each entry describes one way to connect: an endpoint, a credential, and the facts about that endpoint the tests use to decide what to run against it.

servers.description: Every server entry is tested independently. List the same URL twice to test it with a second credential.

name.description: Label used in test names. Defaults to the username and endpoint.

url.description: The WSMan endpoint, for example http://server:5985/wsman or https://server:5986/wsman. The scheme selects HTTP or HTTPS and the port and path are taken from the URL.

username.description: The username to authenticate with, user@REALM for a domain account or the plain name for a local account. Required unless auth only contains certificate.

auth.description: The authentication methods that work for this endpoint and credential. A domain account normally supports kerberos, ntlm and credssp while a local account supports basic, ntlm and credssp. certificate needs client_certificate and is the only method that does not need a username and password.

untrusted_certificate.description: Set when the HTTPS certificate is not trusted by this machine. The tests then disable certificate validation when connecting to this entry.

client_certificate.description: The client certificate to use when auth contains certificate. Either a PFX file or a PEM certificate and key pair.

cert.description: Path to the certificate. A .pfx or .p12 file holds the private key itself, any other extension is a PEM certificate that needs key. Relative paths are resolved from the directory containing the settings file.

key.description: Path to the PEM encoded RSA private key. Required unless cert is a .pfx or .p12 file. Relative paths are resolved from the directory containing the settings file.

password.description: The PFX password, or the password of the PEM private key when it is encrypted.

jea.description: The name of a Just Enough Administration session configuration on this endpoint that runs as a virtual account and exposes a Get-PSWSManJeaUserName function returning [Environment]::UserName, see tools/SetupWinCI.ps1. Enables the JEA test for this entry.

trusted_for_delegation.description: Set when the server is trusted for unconstrained Kerberos delegation. Enables the delegation tests for this entry.
